channel.description: Notes, projects and things I keep learning.

item.title: Telegram notifications from your own processes and applications
item.description: A Telegram group split into topics and a small command so my scripts and applications tell me what went well and, above all, what went wrong.

item.title: My grandmother’s lullaby
item.description: I don't know how long I've been meaning to write about Mil Venecies. This comic, written by my uncle Guti and drawn by my cousin Castri, tells the story of our grandmother Olvido, Guti's mother. It won them the 17th…

item.title: A CMS that never leaves home
item.description: I've been collecting editions of The Hobbit in different languages for years, and until recently the collection's website lived on a Google Site. It worked, but it was far from flexible. Every time a new book arrived I…

item.title: Use symbolic links to avoid duplicates
item.description: The problem with Yakreader Do you have an app that doesn't handle users, and you want several people to use it? That was my situation with Yakreader, my comic and manga reader. Yakreader has no users, and in a reader,…

item.title: A fan that switches itself on
item.description: How I made my server's fan switch on only when the CPU is working, with a Tuya wifi relay controlled locally and a small container that queries Prometheus.

item.title: Mac mini cooling stand
item.description: I rescued a 2012 Mac Mini from the cupboard and turned it into my home server. When it started overheating, I designed a custom stand for it with a fan underneath.

item.title: How to create a Telegram bot
item.description: How I built miBusete, a private Telegram bot that tells you how long until the bus arrives, with no database and no open ports, and what I learnt along the way.

item.title: Another Monday crossed off the calendar
item.description: Another Monday crossed off the calendar. Another trip back up that hill where I feel your absence most, unable to hear you, without you there.

item.title: The tragedy of time relativity
item.description: I have a family that makes me happy, a job I love and great friends. So why do I keep asking myself Steve Jobs' question in front of the mirror? A reflection on routine, weekends that fly by and time as the most precious thing we have.
